title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
description: Storm-0940, a China-state aligned threat actor, has used the AI-driven ARTEX penetration testing framework since September 2026 to automate large-scale attacks targeting hundreds of organizations globally across multiple industries. These attacks have enabled the actor to gain privileged access to cloud infrastructures rapidly, sometimes within three hours of initial targeting. The actor leveraged ARTEX to accelerate scanning, reconnaissance, password spraying, and OAuth application abuse, notably in the ConnectWise supply chain compromise. The activity involved abuse of Microsoft 365 OAuth applications to access customer environments without interactive user sign-in, followed by reconnaissance and privilege escalation attempts via Microsoft Graph. Microsoft confirmed that these attacks did not stem from vulnerabilities in Microsoft corporate systems or products. Microsoft Defender XDR provides detections and hunting queries to identify suspicious activity related to this threat. Customers are advised to review service principal sign-ins and investigate unexpected credential or privilege changes while following published containment guidance.
aiSummary: Storm-0940 is a China-state aligned actor active since 2021, targeting diverse industries for data theft. Starting September 2026, the actor integrated the agentic AI penetration testing framework ARTEX to automate and scale offensive operations globally. ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM system, automates penetration testing workflows from reconnaissance to data exfiltration with minimal human input. Using ARTEX, Storm-0940 accelerated attack phases including scanning, password spraying, and OAuth application abuse, enabling rapid privileged access to cloud environments. The actor exploited compromised OAuth applications to authenticate to Microsoft 365 environments without interactive sign-in, conducting follow-on activities such as reconnaissance, credential changes, and privilege modifications via Microsoft Graph. This campaign included the ConnectWise supply chain compromise affecting multi-tenant applications. Microsoft confirmed no compromise of its own corporate systems or products. Microsoft Defender XDR offers detection capabilities for this threat, and customers should monitor for suspicious Microsoft Graph activity and application credential changes.
aiImpact: The threat actor gained privileged access to multiple organizations' cloud infrastructures, enabling potential persistent access and data exfiltration. The use of AI automation significantly reduced the time from targeting to compromise, increasing the speed and scale of attacks. The ConnectWise supply chain compromise illustrates the risk of downstream impacts from such supply chain attacks. Although Microsoft detected authentication and follow-on activities in affected environments, the presence of these activities does not necessarily confirm data access or exfiltration. The rapid and automated nature of the attacks challenges defenders' ability to respond effectively before the actor establishes persistence.
